physiology:
The traditions seat this code in the immune system, which is not an organ so much as a long quiet conversation running through the whole body. Lymph, marrow, spleen, the lining of the gut, every pore of the skin. Its work is recognition. What is me. What is not me. What belongs here and what is to be turned away. It is the body's oldest reading of a stranger, older than thought, made of chemistry and scent.

The shadow has its bodily floor here. When the reading goes off true, the system mistakes friend for threat and threat for friend. It flares at what would have nourished it and opens the door to what will wear it down. Allergies, low fevers that never quite name themselves, infections that come back. The body argues with rooms it should have welcomed. It welcomes rooms it should have shut. The static of interference is not only in the mind. It is in the cells deciding who to admit, and getting it wrong.

The climb out is also bodily, and it has the texture of an animal calming. Inflammation eases. The skin stops bracing. You walk into a place and your shoulders drop or they do not, and the body has answered before you have framed the question. Recognition returns to the level where it always lived, below speech, in the system that has been smelling the world for you all along.
amino_acid:
Deeper than the organ, this code answers to a single amino acid, Glutamic acid. It is one of the most abundant in the body and one of the busiest. The cells use it to speak to each other. It is the most common excitatory signal in the nervous system, and it is also a central messenger between immune cells when they are deciding what to do about a stranger.

There is a teaching in that, and it sits exactly where this card sits. The code whose shadow is interference and whose gift is recognising your true allies runs on the chemistry of signalling. The whole architecture of who is friend and who is not, in the cells, is made of one molecule passed from one to another, again and again, fast and quiet.

This is why the card keeps coming back to the same instruction in different voices. The reading is not broken, the signal is noisy. The chemistry says it lower than any teaching. The code runs all the way to this: a recognition that is not a decision but a conversation, already happening, in a language the body never had to learn.
